angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 667,872 km at 56.79 pc = 0.16 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 17.6090 +/- 0.0162 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 56.79 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.96 +/- 0.006 solar radii from Bonfanti et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 183579 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671L...8B/abstract): 667,872 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.996 +/- 0.049 solar masses from Bonfanti et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 183579 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671L...8B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5784 +/- 61 K from Bonfanti et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 183579 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671L...8B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonfanti et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 183579 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671L...8B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-183579.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.472, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 183579 (pscomppars): spectral type G2 V, from Gan et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.507.2220G/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 183579 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.038 dex, from Bonfanti et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671L...8B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 183579 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.03386, from Bonfanti et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671L...8B/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 183579 (pscomppars): age 3.1 Gyr, from Bonfanti et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671L...8B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 183579 (pscomppars): rotation period 24.8 d, from Bonfanti et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671L...8B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 183579 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2 km/s, from Nordstrom et al. 2004 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2004A&A...418..989N/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
